taxonomyNote: Sources place this species in Masticophis (Nicholson 2025 via NatureServe), not Coluber.
fieldMarks: Slender snake 36-72 in (90-183 cm) with smooth scales in 15 rows at midbody and a divided anal plate.
Dark brown, grey or blue above with three light grey-to-white stripes on each side; the side stripe is split by a broken or continuous dark band.
behavior: Fast, alert and diurnal; flees to rocks, rodent burrows or shrubs, but cornered individuals often stand their ground and strike.
Active hunter using vision and scent, taking lizards, other snakes, amphibians, nestling birds and rodents; juveniles take insects.
Active mainly April-October in Colorado and Utah; retreats underground or into crevices in cold weather; climbs (terrestrial and arboreal).
habitat: Shrublands, arid grassland, sagebrush flats, canyons, pinyon-juniper and pine-oak woodland, and rocky stream courses; often near ponds and rivers.
Eggs are laid in abandoned small-mammal burrows.
range: Southeastern Washington and southern Idaho south through Oregon, eastern California, Nevada, Utah, western Colorado, Arizona, New Mexico and western and central Texas into northern Mexico; up to about 3,077 m.
